function.name: EventSettingsApi_create_website_alert_config
function.description: Creates a configuration for website alerting within the system, allowing users to define conditions under which alerts should be triggered for a website. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name for the website alert configuration.

description.description: A detailed description for the website alert configuration.

severity.description: The severity level of the alert when triggered.

triggering.description: Flag indicating whether the alert configuration should also trigger an incident.

websiteId.description: The unique identifier of the website for which the alert configuration is created.

tagFilterExpression.description: A boolean expression used to filter the scope of website beacons based on tags.

granularity.description: The evaluation granularity in seconds used for detection of threshold violations.

rule.description: The type of rule this alert configuration pertains to, such as 'traffic spike' or 'downtime'.

threshold.description: The threshold value that, when exceeded, will trigger the alert. This is a float type value.

timeThreshold.description: The time duration in seconds during which the threshold must be exceeded to trigger the alert.

alertChannelIds.description: A list of alert channel IDs defined in Instana to which the alert notifications will be sent.

message.content:
Instana’s public API follows a **major‑minor** scheme similar to many modern SaaS platforms:

| Major Version | Typical Release Period | Key Notes |
|---------------|------------------------|-----------|
| **v1**        | Legacy – still supported but gradually being phased out | Provides most core endpoints you’ll see in older documentation. It remains fully functional for backward compatibility. |
| **v2**        | Current stable release | Adds new features, improved performance, better pagination handling, and more granular filtering options. Most recent SDKs and CLI tooling target `v2`. |

### How to determine what your instance is actually exposing

When you hit the base URL (`https://<your-instana-host>/api`) without specifying a path, Instana returns a small JSON payload containing the available API groups and their URLs. For example:

```bash
curl -u <token>: https://<instana-host>/api/
```

Response snippet:

```json
{
  "apis": {
    "/v1/alerts": "...",
    "/v2/websites": "...",
    ...
  }
}
```

If only `/v1/...` paths appear, your environment is running the legacy API set. If both `/v1/...` and `/v2/...` exist, you’re likely on a mixed deployment where newer services expose `v2`, while some older ones remain behind `v1`.

> **Tip:** In the UI → *Administration* → *API Settings*, there’s usually a toggle or label showing “Using API vX” if you have admin rights.

---

#### Quick sanity check via HTTP headers

Some Instana deployments include the API version in response headers:

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
x-api-version: 2.5
...
```

This header tells you exactly which minor patch of the API you’re hitting.

---

### Bottom line

Most production Instana installations today ship with **API v2** enabled by default, though the old **v1** routes stay alive for backwards compatibility. If you’re unsure, query the root endpoint or inspect the headers returned from any request—you’ll get the definitive answer.
